sections.label: Social cost of smoking
sections.summary: The social cost of smoking amounts to about S$600 million yearly in lost productivity and direct healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The social cost of smoking is not small, amounting to some S$600 million in lost productivity and direct healthcare costs annually.

sections.label: Bill amends Smoking Prohibition Act
sections.summary: The Bill proposes amendments to the Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act, introducing a new section 3A for No Smoking Zones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The Bill before us today, therefore, proposes amendments to the Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act, or referred to as "the Act" later, to strike this balance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We will introduce a new section 3A to expand the scope of the Act so that the National Environment Agency (NEA), with the approval of the Minister can, in addition to prescribing any specific place as a smoking-prohibited place, prescribe a geographical area as an NSZ.

sections.label: Study of Orchard Road DSAs
sections.summary: MEWR studied DSAs in Orchard Road from October 2016 to December 2017, finding a one-third decline in smokers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Between October 2016 and December 2017, the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) had studied the effectiveness of DSAs in the Orchard Road area in reducing smoking activities along the pedestrian thoroughfare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We found that the DSAs led to a one-third decline in the number of smokers along the main thoroughfare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Seventy percent of the non-smokers interviewed also felt that passive tobacco smoke along the main thoroughfare had been reduced after the DSAs were set up.

sections.label: NEA entry into residential common areas
sections.summary: NEA can enter common areas of residential premises only with reasonable belief that an offence was committed there.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: For common areas of residential premises, NEA can enter only if there is reasonable belief that an offence under the Act has been committed there or that evidence of an offence can be found there, such as upon receiving public feedback about unlawful smoking.

sections.label: Prosecuting uncooperative managers
sections.summary: New sections allow NEA to prosecute uncooperative managers for refusing entry or obstructing its officers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The new sections allow NEA to prosecute uncooperative managers for refusing entry or for obstructing its officers in the course of their duty.

sections.label: NEA obtaining evidence
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies that NEA can obtain audio, visual or physical evidence from a smoking-prohibited place for prosecutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The Bill will also clarify that NEA can obtain audio, visual or physical evidence from a smoking-prohibited place necessary for prosecuting suspected breaches in that place.

sections.label: Monitoring NSZ in Orchard Road
sections.summary: The effectiveness of NSZ in Orchard Road will be monitored before considering extending it to other areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Following the implementation of NSZ in Orchard Road, we will monitor its effectiveness before considering whether to extend the regime to other areas.

sections.label: Orchard Road smoke-free designation
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments will help designate most of the Orchard Road precinct as smoke-free, for more comfortable leisure and shopping.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the amendments in the Bill that will help designate most of the Orchard Road precinct as a smoke-free area, I believe more Singaporeans and tourists, especially families with children, can look forward to having a more comfortable leisure and shopping experience.

sections.label: Residential homes out of smoking regulation
sections.summary: The speaker is disappointed that residential homes remain outside the authorities' regulation on smoking.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Moreover, I am disappointed to learn that residential homes remain out of the authorities’ regulation when it comes to smoking.

sections.label: HDB neighbour cigarette smoke conflicts
sections.summary: Conflicts between HDB neighbours over cigarette smoke crossing into other houses are increasingly rising.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Conflicts between HDB neighbours over cigarette smoke crossing over into other houses are increasingly on the rise.

sections.label: Restricting tobacco sales in Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker says heavily restricting tobacco sales should be looked into, as reduced accessibility would remove enforcement worries.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If accessibility to cigarettes is greatly reduced, then we need not worry about enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is high time to look into heavily restricting tobacco sales in Singapore.

sections.label: Restricting sales and raising tobacco tax
sections.summary: The speaker urges restricting tobacco sales more and raising tobacco tax, using revenue to help smokers quit for a smoke-free nation.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Once the smoker is addicted, it will be very difficult to kick the habit.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should consider restricting tobacco sales even more and increase tobacco tax.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the additional tax revenue, we can help smokers to stop smoking.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In English): But we need stronger measures to fulfil our vision of a smoke-free nation, not for the glory of being the first nation to achieve it, not to become another glowing statistic, but for the well-being of the current generation of Singaporeans and beyond.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke risks
sections.summary: Most cigarette smoke becomes second-hand smoke, which has no risk-free exposure level and contains at least 60 cancer-causing chemicals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Eighty-five percent to 90% of the smoke in every cigarette ends up as second-hand smoke and there is no risk-free level of exposure to second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The World Health Organization has reported that second-hand smoke contains at least 60 cancer-causing chemicals.

sections.label: Smoke-free home quitting study
sections.summary: A nationwide study found people in smoke-free homes were 60% more likely to quit smoking for at least 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to a nationwide study they conducted, people who lived in homes where smoking was prohibited were 60% more likely to quit smoking for at least 30 days, compared to people without this prohibition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Chiyoda-ku City in Tokyo has banned smoking while walking.

sections.label: Enforcement powers and fines
sections.summary: Officers may enter, search, seize and film without warrant, with fines of $2,000 and $5,000 for obstruction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: More specifically, to ascertain if a place has contravened the Act, officers are able to enter, inspect and search places, seize documents or materials, take possession of belongings, and photograph or film without a warrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A maximum fine of $2,000 is imposed on first offenders and $5,000 on repeat offenders who obstruct authorised officers exercising these powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While some powers of entry are necessary for effective enforcement and to achieve better outcomes for people affected by second-hand smoke, the scope of powers and the maximum fine imposed might appear to some to be excessive.

sections.label: Privacy versus broad powers
sections.summary: The speaker asks what measures would prevent abuse of such broad powers, balancing privacy concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, this has to be balanced against privacy concerns, and I would like to ask what measures would be in place to prevent the abuse of such broad powers.

sections.label: Enforcement challenge in smoke-free areas
sections.summary: Enforcement will be a real challenge even though smoking in these smoke-free areas is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this case, enforcement is going to be a real challenge even though it is an offence for a person to smoke in these smoke-free areas.

sections.label: Time for designated smoking facility
sections.summary: Managers and owners of specified places should be given sufficient time to set up a designated smoking facility.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sufficient time should be provided for managers and owners of the specified places to set up a designated smoking facility.

sections.label: Snap Smoking app and penalties
sections.summary: Proposes a Snap Smoking app for real-time reporting and a review of penalties for law breaches affecting non-smokers.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similar to Snap Safe apps introduced by MOM for snapping unsafe work practices, we can also create Snap Smoking apps to empower Singaporeans to report such violations real time.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is a need to review the level of penalty for those who breach the law.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current penalty does not send a stern warning to those who are affecting the non-smokers who are in most danger of passive smoke.

sections.label: Smoking rate and smoker feedback
sections.summary: Smoking rate hovered between 12% and 14% over 10 years, reaching 12% last year, with smokers unhappy about measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the last 10 years, our population’s smoking rate had been hovering between 12% and 14%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Last year, it was at 12%, the lowest to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I have been receiving feedback from smokers who are very unhappy and who are asking for a limit to the number of measures against smoking, including increasing the tobacco excise duty by 10% in this year’s Budget.

sections.label: Reaching smoking rate below 10%
sections.summary: States that with all these measures, a smoking rate below 10% will definitely be reached before long.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With all these measures, before long, we will definitely be able to reach a smoking rate below 10%.

sections.label: Designating NSZs
sections.summary: One of the key amendments in the Bill will allow the Government to designate NSZs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One of the key amendments in the Bill will allow the Government to designate NSZs.

sections.label: Stronger enforcement officer powers
sections.summary: Supports giving enforcement officers stronger regulatory powers, including powers of entry and permits to take photographs and videos.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Naturally, I also support the move to provide stronger regulatory powers to our enforcement officers to conduct thorough investigations without hindrance, such as the powers of entry and permits to take photographs and videos as part of their inspections.

sections.label: Banning smoke in residential areas
sections.summary: Proposes that the Minister consider forbidding the spread of cigarette smoke in residential areas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I have a proposal that I hope the Minister can consider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should forbid the spread of cigarette smoke in residential areas.

sections.label: Smoke detected outside flat
sections.summary: If smoke is detected outside the flat, the resident should be considered to have violated the law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If smoke is detected outside of the flat, the resident should then be considered to have violated the law.

sections.label: NSZ questions and manager offence
sections.summary: The passage asks about prioritised public areas, implementation timeframe, common staircases and corridors as NSZs, and states a manager offence.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: One, what are the public areas in Singapore that will be prioritised by NEA to be designated as NSZs?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Two, is there a timeframe in which the new NSZs will be implemented throughout Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Four, to reduce the probability of second-hand smoke in residential estates, especially for HDB dwellings, will the common staircases and common corridors be marked as NSZs for a start?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Five, the Bill stated that a manager of a specified place who fails to ensure that the smoking facility in the specified place complies with the prescribed requirement commits an offence.

sections.label: Enforcement capacity and education
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on enforcement team strength and whether capacity suffices for patrolling new specified places.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In light of the feedback mentioned above, I believe there is still some way to go for us to look into beefing up enforcement and, more importantly, educating people about the efforts in creating a smoke-free environment for all, especially our future generation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would like, therefore, to seek some clarification on the current strength of the enforcement team.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Would the current capacity be sufficient to deal with the patrolling and enforcement that need to be carried out at the new specified places where smoking will be prohibited?

sections.label: Regulating smoking in private spaces
sections.summary: The passage asks whether rules could be enhanced to regulate smokers in private spaces affecting others.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In relation to the issue of smoking in residential homes, are there any enhancements to rules that could be put in place to regulate the conduct of smokers in private spaces which impacts on others?

sections.label: Penalties for second-hand smoke
sections.summary: The passage asks whether penalties could be considered when second-hand tobacco smoke is expelled out of a residential home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this regard, could we consider some penalties when second-hand tobacco smoke is expelled out of a residential home?

sections.label: Orchard Road NSZ initiative
sections.summary: The NSZ in Orchard Road is a new initiative.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The NSZ in Orchard Road is a new initiative.

sections.label: DSA count in NSZ
sections.summary: About 40 DSAs can be found across the prospective NSZ today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Today, about 40 DSAs can be found across the prospective NSZ.

sections.label: Orchard Road NSZ smoking ban
sections.summary: Once in force, every public place in the Orchard Road NSZ would be smoking-prohibited, so smokers could not light up while walking the shopping belt.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Once the Orchard Road NSZ is in force, every public place within the zone would be smoking-prohibited, and smokers would not be able to light up while walking along the shopping belt.

sections.label: NSZ coming into force
sections.summary: The NSZ will be brought into force in the coming months, with details provided in due course.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The NSZ will be brought into force in the coming months and details will be provided in due course.

sections.label: NEA engagement and enforcement
sections.summary: NEA has been engaging business owners about the Orchard Road NSZ and will calibrate enforcement capacity according to the situation on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NEA has been engaging business owners about the Orchard Road NSZ and will calibrate its enforcement capacity according to the situation on the ground.

sections.label: Thermal cameras to deter smoking
sections.summary: NEA is exploring thermal cameras to deter indiscriminate smoking, especially at corridors, lift lobbies and staircase landings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NEA is also exploring the use of thermal cameras to deter indiscriminate smoking, such as the one that Miss Cheryl Chan raised earlier, especially at corridors, lift lobbies and staircase landings, which other Members had also raised.

sections.label: Smoking corners and NSZ closures
sections.summary: Since June 2017 smoking corners have been disallowed in new food establishments, and outdoor smoking areas in the NSZ will have to close.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In the case of smoking facilities located within food establishments, such as coffee shops, I would like to update Mr Louis Ng and Ms Joan Pereira that since June 2017, smoking corners have been disallowed in new food establishments across the island.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: When the Orchard Road NSZ comes into effect, outdoor smoking areas at food establishments within the NSZ will also have to close.

sections.label: NEA entry and inspection powers
sections.summary: New section 4A lets NEA enter and inspect smoking-prohibited premises, and managers refusing entry commit an offence under section 4B.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The new section 4A gives NEA the powers to enter and inspect smoking-prohibited premises, as not all of these premises are freely accessible to the public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Managers who refuse NEA entry would now be liable for an offence under the new section 4B.

sections.label: Penalties for abuse of officers
sections.summary: Amendments set fines of up to $2,000 for a first offence and $5,000 for later offences, or up to three months' imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: These amendments will also underscore our firm stance against abuse and threats made against our officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Those found guilty of such acts will face fines of up to $2,000 for a first offence, and $5,000 for a second or subsequent offence, or a maximum of three months' imprisonment, or both.

sections.label: NEA smoking enforcement tickets
sections.summary: NEA issued 22,000 smoking tickets last year, and Members called for NEA to be more active and responsive in enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Last year, NEA issued 22,000 tickets for smoking, and there are calls from Members for NEA to be even more active and responsive in undertaking its enforcement duties.

sections.label: Orchard Road no-smoking zone first
sections.summary: The NSZ is implemented first in Orchard Road to monitor outcomes, given concerns about non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For setting up of more DSPs, to the Member's comment about what if we have an NSZ and they do not comply, then it will not be effective, it is precisely because of this that we are only implementing the NSZ first in Orchard Road because we want to monitor the outcomes.

sections.label: Thermal cameras not acquired
sections.summary: NEA is not acquiring the thermal cameras itself.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Regarding thermal cameras, we are not acquiring the thermal cameras ourselves.

sections.label: NEA powers in private estates
sections.summary: Section 4 allows NEA officers to enter, inspect and investigate common areas of private residential estates that are smoking-prohibited when they reasonably believe an offence occurred.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Section 4 actually explicitly allows NEA officers to enter, inspect, investigate in common areas which are smoking prohibited areas of private residential estates when they reasonably believe that there is an offence being committed or had been committed there, or that there is evidence that a smoking offence has been committed.

sections.label: Enforcement manpower and surveillance equipment
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State about plans to expand the enforcement team, manpower on the ground, and investment in surveillance equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even as we expand these areas, I want to ask the Senior Minister of State whether there are plans to step up or expand the enforcement team, whether there is enough manpower on the ground to do it as, otherwise, there is no deterrent, and also whether there are investments into surveillance equipment to also step up the enforcement there.

sections.label: Thermal cameras and manager accountability
sections.summary: A tender was called to use thermal cameras for smoking offences, and the amendment will require managers to be accountable for their premises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Earlier, I did mention that we are now looking – in fact, we had called for a tender – to use thermal cameras with regard to smoking offences or smoking violations, say, at lift lobbies, staircase landings and so on, to help us with our enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: At the end of the day, as I have said many times in my speech, we need the community to come together to help us with this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, this amendment to this Act will also explicitly require the managers to be accountable, to be responsible for their premises, to ask the smoking offender to stop smoking or to leave their premises.

sections.label: Smoking rate figures
sections.summary: The speaker states the rate was 12% last year, down from 23% long ago to about 14% and then 12%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Earlier in my opening speech, I said that last year, it was 12%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: It has come down from 23% long time ago to about 14% and then 12%.

sections.label: Trained CVs number
sections.summary: The speaker states there are currently about 400 CVs who are trained.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Regarding the CVs, we currently have about 400 CVs who are trained.
